$comment: Reviewed SLO baseline for scripts/restore-drill.js. Every entry carries a written reason, never a bare number: a duration without the dataset and machine it was measured on is not an SLO. Rewritten deliberately with `node scripts/restore-drill.js --update`, which refuses to write from any run that found a correctness failure or injected a fault — the diff is meant to be reviewed. Exceeding toleranceFactor is reported as a WARN and does NOT fail the drill; see FR-8 in the runbook for why.

inventory.reason: Measured by the drill on the local Docker stack after the migrator applied 0_baseline and the demo seed ran (tenant demo, school VOLTAIRE). tableCount drift is a hard failure: a table dropped from schema.prisma vanishes from the source AND the restore and would compare equal for ever. Row totals move with the seed and are reported, not enforced.

ledger.reason: Every directory under apps/api/prisma/migrations must come back in the restored _prisma_migrations, finished and not rolled back. A restore without the migration history is a restore of the data, not of the database. 20260809120000_tenant_timezone was added by S-E04-5 (additive `tenant.timezone`, expand-only) and is recorded here by hand as part of that review — this list is a reviewed record, so a migration reaching disk without reaching this file is exactly the drift the check exists to catch. 20260813120000_tenant_rls_policies was added by S-E01-2b (RLS: ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus a tenant_isolation policy on the 44 tenant_id tables, and DML grants to the non-owner role app_user) and is recorded here by hand as part of that review — it reached disk in run 52 and this check caught its absence from this file on the very same run, which is the mechanism working rather than a nuisance. TWO RESTORE-SPECIFIC CONSEQUENCES, recorded because a bare name in a list would hide them: (1) pg_dump does emit CREATE POLICY and ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so a restore reproduces the policies — but it does NOT recreate the cluster-wide role app_user, which lives outside the database, so a restore onto a cluster without that role comes back with the policies intact and the grants silently absent; (2) the durations below were measured against a two-migration ledger on a database with no policies at all, and RLS adds per-row predicate evaluation to nothing here because the local database holds zero rows — so they are not invalidated by this migration, but they will need re-measuring from a seeded database before they mean anything about a restore under RLS. 20260813180000_tenant_rls_derived_policies was added by S-E01-2c (PF-183: an FK-path tenant_isolation policy plus per-table DML grants on the five tenant-DERIVED tables — announcement_receipt, branding, grade_revision, import_row, user_role — which carry no tenant_id of their own) and is recorded here by hand as part of that review. It reached disk in run 53, and this check caught its absence from this file on that same run — the SECOND consecutive run in which it has done so, which is worth stating plainly: the mechanism is not merely working, it is now the standing way this class of drift is found, because the agents that write a migration cannot see this file from where they work (PF-80). ONE FURTHER RESTORE-SPECIFIC CONSEQUENCE, and it is specific to the FK-path shape rather than to RLS in general: a derived policy's predicate names its PARENT table, and a policy expression is evaluated AS THE CALLING USER, so a restore is only faithful if it brings back BOTH tables AND app_user's SELECT privilege on every named parent. A restore that reproduces the five child tables while dropping a parent grant does not fail loudly — every read of the child returns `permission denied` raised from inside the policy, which reads like a broken feature rather than a broken restore. The durations below are again not invalidated (the local database holds zero rows, so there is no per-row predicate to evaluate), and the same caveat stands: they mean nothing about a restore under RLS until they are re-measured from a seeded database. 20260814120000_outbox_event_tenant_scope was added by S-E01-2d (PF-185 / ADR-044: outbox_event, the last base table outside every policy class, receives a DENORMALISED tenant_id column, an ON DELETE CASCADE foreign key to tenant, a leading index (tenant_id, status, created_at), the ordinary tenant_isolation policy and a SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE grant to app_user — deliberately NOT DELETE) and is recorded here by hand as part of that review. It reached disk in run 55, and this check caught its absence from this file on that same run — the THIRD consecutive run in which it has done so. That is no longer a near-miss worth noting, it is the standing mechanism by which this class of drift is found, and it recurs because the agents that write a migration cannot see this file from where they work (PF-80). THIS ENTRY IS THE FIRST THAT IS NOT PURELY ADDITIVE DDL, and the restore consequences differ in kind from the two RLS entries above rather than merely in degree. (1) tableCount is UNCHANGED at 55 and must stay so: this migration adds a COLUMN, not a table, so a tableCount move here would be real drift and not this story. (2) Unlike the FK-path five, this table's policy predicate names NO parent, so there is no parent SELECT grant a restore can silently drop — the failure mode ADR-042 warned about does not apply here, and saying otherwise by analogy would be a copy-paste of the previous entry's reasoning onto a different shape. (3) What IS newly at risk is the ATTRIBUTION ITSELF: tenant_id on outbox_event is DATA, not a derivation, because aggregate_type/aggregate_id are polymorphic and unconstrained. A restore that loses or truncates that column cannot recompute it from anything else in the dump — there is no join that recovers it. The backfill in the migration is therefore NOT a repair path for a bad restore; it is fail-loud by design and RAISES on any multi-tenant database carrying orphan rows rather than guessing. (4) app_user still lives outside the database, exactly as recorded for the two entries above, so a restore onto a cluster lacking that role still comes back with the policy intact and the grant silently absent. The durations are again not invalidated (zero rows, no per-row predicate) and carry the same standing caveat.

dumpMs.reason: Measured by `node scripts/restore-drill.js --update` — pg_dump -Fc of the whole database. Windows 11 host, Docker Desktop, postgres:15-alpine, the seeded demo dataset recorded under `inventory`.

restoreMs.reason: Measured by `node scripts/restore-drill.js --update` — pg_restore --exit-on-error into a fresh scratch database. Windows 11 host, Docker Desktop, postgres:15-alpine, the seeded demo dataset recorded under `inventory`.

verifyMs.reason: Measured by `node scripts/restore-drill.js --update` — rebuilding the manifest from the restored database and comparing it. Windows 11 host, Docker Desktop, postgres:15-alpine, the seeded demo dataset recorded under `inventory`.

totalMs.reason: Measured by `node scripts/restore-drill.js --update` — the whole cycle, including manifest builds and cleanup. Windows 11 host, Docker Desktop, postgres:15-alpine, the seeded demo dataset recorded under `inventory`.

toleranceFactor.reason: Wide on purpose. The measurement is a developer laptop against a Docker volume under variable load; a tight factor would make the drill flake, and a gate that flakes is re-run until green instead of read. Exceeding it is a WARN, never a non-zero exit.
